capsuleTopic.title: Baptism of Jesus
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Jordan · John · Spirit · voice · witness
capsuleTopic.orientation: Enter the baptism through each Gospel witness, then follow the words, actions, testimony, aftermath, and later memory that Scripture places around it.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Notice what each witness says about Jesus, John, water, Spirit, voice, recognition, testing, and the Event’s later memory—and what each witness leaves unstated.

nodes.note: The speaker says the Lord’s Spirit is on him because the LORD has anointed him to announce good news and release.
nodes.title: The Spirit and anointing commission proclamation

nodes.note: The LORD sends a messenger to prepare the way before the desired lord and covenant messenger comes.
nodes.title: A messenger prepares for a sudden arrival

nodes.note: The closing oracle calls Israel to remember Moses and promises Elijah before the great day.
nodes.title: Elijah is promised before the day of the LORD

payload.title: Voices before the Jordan

payload.description: Acts repeatedly locates Jesus’ ministry, witness, and the promise of the Spirit in relation to John’s baptism.

nodes.note: The risen Jesus teaches about God’s Kingdom and tells the apostles to wait in Jerusalem for the Father’s promise.
nodes.title: Jesus contrasts John’s water baptism with the Spirit promise

nodes.note: Peter requires a replacement witness who accompanied the group from John’s baptism until Jesus’ ascension.
nodes.title: Apostolic witness is traced from John’s baptism

nodes.note: Peter summarizes the word proclaimed through Judea beginning from Galilee after John’s baptism.
nodes.title: Peter begins Jesus’ public story after John’s baptism

nodes.note: Paul retells Israel’s story through David to the promised Savior, then names John’s baptism of repentance before Jesus’ coming.
nodes.title: Paul places John before Jesus’ coming

nodes.note: Apollos is eloquent, powerful in Scripture, instructed in the Lord’s way, and fervent, yet knows only John’s baptism.
nodes.title: Apollos teaches accurately while knowing only John’s baptism

nodes.note: Paul meets disciples who have not heard about the Holy Spirit and asks into what they were baptized.
nodes.title: Disciples of John receive fuller instruction

nodes.note: Peter explains the Spirit’s coming on Gentiles by remembering the Lord’s contrast between John’s water baptism and baptism in the Holy Spirit.
nodes.title: Peter remembers Jesus’ words about John and the Spirit

payload.title: The event in apostolic proclamation

payload.description: Jesus asks leaders to account for John’s baptism, and later disciples remember the baptism as part of Jesus’ public beginning.

nodes.note: When leaders challenge Jesus’ authority, he asks whether John’s baptism came from heaven or humans.
nodes.title: Jesus asks leaders to judge John’s baptism

nodes.note: Chief priests, scribes, and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he answers with a question about John’s baptism.
nodes.title: Mark links Jesus’ authority question to John’s baptism

nodes.note: While Jesus teaches in the Temple, leaders demand the source of his authority; he asks about John’s baptism.
nodes.title: Luke preserves the same authority deadlock

nodes.note: Jesus claims all authority and sends the eleven to make disciples of all nations.
nodes.title: The risen Jesus commissions baptism among all nations

payload.title: The baptism becomes a public question

payload.description: Later Scripture reuses baptism, water, Spirit, death, burial, clothing, washing, and appeal language without collapsing those texts into the Jordan event.

nodes.note: Paul asks whether grace permits continued sin and answers by describing baptism into Christ Jesus and into his death.
nodes.title: Baptism is described through death, burial, and new life

nodes.note: Paul contrasts custody under law with faith’s arrival and calls believers God’s children through faith in Christ Jesus.
nodes.title: Baptism is joined to putting on Christ

nodes.note: The letter locates divine fullness in Christ and believers’ fullness in him.
nodes.title: Baptism joins burial, raising, forgiveness, and victory

nodes.note: Christ suffers once, is made alive in the Spirit, and the passage moves through imprisoned spirits, Noah, ark, and flood.
nodes.title: Noah’s water is carried into a baptism statement

nodes.note: The letter recalls former folly and hostility, then says God’s kindness appeared and salvation came by mercy rather than righteous works.
nodes.title: Washing and renewal are attributed to divine mercy

nodes.note: James and John ask for honored seats; Jesus asks whether they can drink his cup or receive his baptism.
nodes.title: Jesus names a cup and baptism of suffering

nodes.note: Jesus speaks of casting fire on the earth and of a baptism he must undergo, saying he is distressed until it is completed.
nodes.title: Jesus speaks of a baptism still ahead

payload.title: Baptism language after the event

payload.description: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John preserve distinct evidence: arrival, reluctance, prayer, opened heaven, Spirit, voice, sign, testimony, and following.

nodes.note: Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized; John resists, Jesus answers, and the baptism proceeds.
nodes.title: Jesus comes to John and speaks of fulfilling righteousness

nodes.note: Jesus comes from Nazareth, is baptized by John, and immediately sees the heavens torn open and the Spirit descending.
nodes.title: The heavens are torn open over Jesus

nodes.note: After all the people are baptized, Jesus is baptized and prays; heaven opens.
nodes.title: Jesus prays as heaven opens

nodes.note: John calls Jesus God’s Lamb, says Jesus ranks before him, and explains that the purpose of his water baptism was Israel’s recognition.
nodes.title: John identifies Jesus by a descending and remaining Spirit

nodes.note: John again identifies Jesus as God’s Lamb, two disciples follow, and Andrew brings Simon.
nodes.title: John’s testimony sends disciples after Jesus

payload.title: The baptism in four witnesses

payload.description: Each Synoptic witness carries Jesus from baptism into wilderness testing and the beginning of public proclamation.

nodes.note: Immediately after the baptism, the Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness where the tempter repeatedly challenges his sonship.
nodes.title: The Spirit leads the beloved Son into testing

nodes.note: The Spirit immediately drives Jesus into the wilderness for forty days with Satan, wild animals, and angels.
nodes.title: The Spirit drives Jesus into wilderness before proclamation

nodes.note: Jesus returns from the Jordan full of the Holy Spirit and is led in the wilderness through forty days of temptation.
nodes.title: Full of the Spirit, Jesus is led and tested

nodes.note: Jesus returns in the Spirit’s power, reads Isaiah 61, and announces its fulfillment in the listeners’ hearing.
nodes.title: Spirit-anointed proclamation reaches Nazareth

payload.title: From Jordan into testing and proclamation

payload.description: John calls Israel to repent, baptizes in water, and points beyond his own work to the coming one.

nodes.note: John appears in Judea’s wilderness, announces the Kingdom, baptizes confessing people, confronts leaders, and speaks of one stronger.
nodes.title: John calls for repentance and points to the coming one

nodes.note: Mark opens with prophetic words, John’s baptism of repentance for forgiveness, and testimony about the stronger one.
nodes.title: Mark joins messenger, wilderness, forgiveness, and promise

nodes.note: The word of God comes to John in a named political and priestly setting; he announces repentance, answers crowds, and denies being the Christ.
nodes.title: Luke dates John’s call and records its social demands

nodes.note: John tells Jerusalem’s delegation that he is not the Christ, Elijah, or the prophet, then identifies himself with Isaiah’s voice.
nodes.title: John denies three identities and names a present unknown one

payload.title: John prepares the way

payload.description: Later exchanges preserve John’s testimony, declining prominence, uncertainty, imprisonment, and death.

nodes.note: Jesus’ disciples baptize while John is still baptizing; a purification dispute prompts concern about growing attention to Jesus.
nodes.title: A baptism dispute leads John to speak of increase and decrease

nodes.note: Jesus learns that the Pharisees heard he was making and baptizing more disciples than John.
nodes.title: The disciples’ baptizing becomes publicly noticed

nodes.note: From prison John sends disciples to ask Jesus whether he is the coming one.
nodes.title: John asks whether Jesus is the coming one

nodes.note: John’s disciples report Jesus’ deeds; John sends two to ask whether he is the coming one.
nodes.title: Luke preserves John’s question after Jesus heals

nodes.note: Herod imprisons John because John challenges his marriage; a banquet promise leads to John’s beheading.
nodes.title: John is executed after confronting Herod

nodes.note: Mark reports Herod’s puzzled protection of John, Herodias’ hostility, the banquet, and the forced execution.
nodes.title: Mark expands Herod’s fear and John’s death

payload.title: John keeps pointing beyond himself

payload.description: The transfiguration and its later memory repeat beloved-Son language in a new setting and preserve a distinct eyewitness claim.

nodes.note: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John; Moses and Elijah appear, and a bright cloud overshadows them.
nodes.title: The beloved-Son voice is heard on the mountain

nodes.note: Peter denies following myths and describes being an eyewitness of Jesus’ majesty.
nodes.title: Peter remembers hearing the majestic voice

payload.title: The voice heard again
